claude.sample_unit: patient education topics (37 ALA and 72 AAO-HNS)

links.outcome: Readability (FRE, FK grade) of patient education materials before vs after ChatGPT simplification
links.effect: Overall FRE scores and FK grades improved significantly after ChatGPT translation (p < 0.001) by ChatGPT scoring; Word also showed significant improvement for AAO-HNS materials overall (p < 0.001), but not for individual topics or subspecialty categories. ChatGPT exaggerated the change versus Word.
links.quote: Overall FRE scores and FK grades demonstrated significant improvements following translation of materials, as scored by ChatGPT (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Whether LLM simplification makes patient education materials more plain-language and readable
links.effect: Materials were written above recommended reading levels; ChatGPT translation significantly improved FRE and FK scores (p < 0.001), though ChatGPT self-scoring exaggerated the improvement relative to Word.
links.quote: Otolaryngology patient education materials were found to be written at higher reading levels than recommended.

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM to measure readability scores of existing patient education materials

screen.practice: reading-level constraint prompting for patient materials
screen.reason: The study tests an AI prompt guardrail/practice (prompting ChatGPT to simplify patient education materials to a 5th-grade reading level) and evaluates whether it successfully alters readability metrics compared to a standard measurement tool (Word).
